scenes.narration: A train cannot steer. Its wheels are fixed to the axle, so the rails decide where it goes. When a train needs to change tracks, the track itself has to move.
That is the job of the switch. At its entrance sit two tapered rails, the points, lying between the fixed stock rails.
A switch motor or hand lever slides the points sideways, pressing one against a stock rail and opening a gap beside the other.

The wheel flange follows the closed point, guiding the train straight ahead or onto the diverging track. Further on, the routes cross at the frog, a V-shaped casting with a gap that lets the flange pass through.
A guard rail opposite the frog keeps the wheel on line. If the points are set against the train, it can split the switch or derail, so the route is locked and signalled before the train arrives.
